text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL NEEDS MORE IMAGINATION TO BOOST EXPORTS
Brazil does not know how to take advantage of opportunities in the United States market, the most open in the world, in order to boost exports, U.S. Commerce Department figures show.
-- WTO: ZERO TARIFF WOULD HELP POOREST COUNTRIES
Richard Blackhurst, chief economist at the World Trade Organization, defended WTO policies, saying developing nations would receive $75 billion a year if all tariffs were reduced to zero.
-- CPMF CHECK-TAX SCARES OFF $12 BLN IN FOREIGN CAPITAL

Foreign investors, shunning the new CPMF check tax on financial transactions to be implemented in 1997, are pulling their money out of Brazil at a rate of $60 million a day, or $12 billion by the end of the year, the Central Bank said.
O GLOBO
-- PANEL CONCLUDES CONGRESSMAN SHOULD BE OUSTED
A commission investigating charges Rep. Pedrihno Abrao sought a bribe from a construction firm has concluded the evidence is strong enough to warrant that he be stripped of his post.
-- FINANCE MINISTRY ASKS RIO TO EXPLAIN TARIFF HIKE
Brazil's Finance Ministry has asked Rio de Janeiro state's government to explain why subway, train and ferry fares have been hiked 66.66 percent.
-- SENATE APPROVES AGRARIAN REFORM BILL

The Brazilian Senate, in a bid to address one of the country's most gripping social problems, unanimously approved an agrarian reform bill that reduces the time it takes to expropriate land for distribution to landless farmers.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- CONGRESS' LOWER HOUSE SCRAPS PRISON FOR DRUG USER
Congress' lower house has approved a bill that would eliminate prison terms for drug users. The measure now goes to the Senate.
-- BUDGET PANEL CUTS QUESTIONED REVENUE ITEM

Congress' joint budget commission has cut from its 1997 spending proposal some 42 million reais in funds set aside for a construction project in northeastern Brazil that is at the heart of a corruption scandal.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
